correctness.rationale: For n=2m+1>=5, nondegenerate affine diameters correspond to edge E_i and its opposite support vertex v_(i+m+1). The locus for that edge is precisely triangle T_i=conv(E_i,v_(i+m+1)). Two triangle sides occupy each longest-diagonal boundary on its center side, so on a generic radial traversal the overlap count decreases by two, from n centrally to 1 near the polygon edge. All odd intermediate levels have open cells. The n-overlap is the intersection of the n center-side diagonal halfplanes; their supporting lines are R sin(pi/(2n)) from origin and normals evenly spaced, yielding inradius and circumradius R sin(pi/(2n))/cos(pi/n). Area ratio to P_n equals sin^2(pi/(2n))/cos^2(pi/n), asymptotically pi^2/(4n^2). A finite union of diagonals is excluded. n=5 reduces to the known central pentagon.
